reference.source: Scriver's OMMBID (Online Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease)
clinicalPearls: Represents the severe end of mevalonate kinase deficiency, in which the enzyme mevalonate kinase (MVK) in the cholesterol/isoprenoid biosynthesis pathway is markedly impaired
The milder allelic phenotype is hyperimmunoglobulinaemia D syndrome (HIDS), a hereditary periodic fever syndrome, so both share recurrent inflammatory febrile attacks
Severe disease features recurrent fevers with lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, rash, and arthralgia, plus failure to thrive, developmental delay, ataxia, and dysmorphism
The biochemical hallmark is markedly elevated urinary mevalonic acid, especially during crises, unlike most organic acidurias where the diagnostic metabolite is downstream

The autoinflammatory phenotype is thought to stem from deficient production of isoprenoid intermediates such as geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate, impairing protein prenylation and dysregulating inflammatory signalling
Attacks may be provoked by vaccination, infection, or stress, and management involves anti-inflammatory and interleukin-1-directed strategies alongside supportive care
Inheritance is autosomal recessive, and cataracts and progressive neurological impairment can occur in severe cases
reference.pathophysiology: Mevalonate kinase phosphorylates mevalonate, an early committed step in the biosynthesis of cholesterol and non-sterol isoprenoids. Severe deficiency causes mevalonic acid to accumulate and be excreted in large amounts, while downstream isoprenoid products, including those needed for protein prenylation (such as geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate), are relatively depleted. Reduced prenylation of small regulatory proteins is believed to activate inflammasome-driven interleukin-1 production, explaining the recurrent autoinflammatory fevers. The combination of substrate accumulation and deficient isoprenoid end-products underlies both the systemic inflammation and the neurodevelopmental and dysmorphic features of the severe form.
additionalDifferentials: Other hereditary periodic fever syndromes (familial Mediterranean fever, TRAPS, cryopyrin-associated syndromes)
Other organic acidurias presenting with encephalopathy and failure to thrive
Lymphoproliferative or malignant disease causing fevers and hepatosplenomegaly
Congenital infection in the neonatal period
additionalInvestigations: Urine organic acids demonstrating raised mevalonic acid, especially during febrile crises
Serum immunoglobulin D and A levels (often elevated in the milder phenotype)
Molecular analysis of the MVK gene
Neuroimaging and ophthalmological assessment for cerebellar and lens involvement
redFlags: Severe recurrent inflammatory crises with dehydration and systemic compromise
Progressive neurological deterioration, ataxia, or developmental regression
Failure to thrive with hepatosplenomegaly in infancy
reference.prognosis: The severe mevalonic aciduria form carries significant morbidity and mortality, with recurrent crises, neurological impairment, and failure to thrive, whereas the milder periodic fever phenotype has a better outlook. Interleukin-1-directed therapy has improved control of inflammatory attacks.
pitfalls: Attributing recurrent fevers to infection alone and missing an autoinflammatory metabolic cause
Not sampling urine organic acids during a crisis when mevalonic acid excretion peaks
Overlooking the neurodevelopmental and ophthalmological complications of severe disease
Failing to anticipate vaccination or infection as attack triggers
references: Scriver's OMMBID: mevalonate kinase deficiency and mevalonic aciduria
Nyhan, Atlas of Inherited Metabolic Diseases
management: Control the recurrent inflammatory attacks with interleukin-1-directed therapy using anakinra or canakinumab
Treat acute flares with corticosteroids or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs alongside supportive care during crises
Provide supportive neurodevelopmental care with physiotherapy, developmental support, and nutritional and feeding support for failure to thrive
Manage the ophthalmological and cerebellar features, including cataract and ataxia
Undertake surveillance for secondary AA amyloidosis with sustained control of inflammation
Consider haematopoietic stem cell transplantation in severe refractory disease
Coordinate metabolic, immunology, and neurology multidisciplinary care and offer genetic counselling for autosomal recessive MVK inheritance
